advice: Propose a guarded n=512 fast path that uses the existing panel32 helper once per 32-row band, but moves the 16-band loop and parameter setup into a new single-entry assembly wrapper. Keep one SME entry/exit and one 64 KiB scratch allocation around the loop; for each band set [4]=B, [10]=A+r*512, [16]=C+r*512, with all other parameter fields zero. Reuse the helper’s existing pack and 16-column-tile body, resetting its input and output pointers and pack cursor for each band. This is distinct from the measured sixteen-call wrapper: it changes helper structure to avoid repeated ABI setup and SME transitions while retaining the supplied computation. It is a hypothesis only; it may add loop and pointer overhead, and it still packs each band. Preserve the original full512 path for other sizes and as a fallback. Checks: establish byte-identical assembly for the unmodified helper before editing; audit callee-saved registers, stack alignment, scratch lifetime, and SME entry/exit placement; then validate n=512 full GEMM output, output overwrite, unchanged inputs, n<=0, and general sizes/tails against the 0.002 tolerance. Measure fresh paired controls under unchanged power settings. Do not treat the prior sixteen-call results as evidence for this changed source.
risks: The source feasibility review describes the loop structure, but the one-entry wrapper has not been implemented or validated. Register preservation, stack cursor resets, or panel pointer mapping errors could corrupt output or violate the ABI. Fewer SME transitions do not establish higher throughput; full-GEMM gains remain unmeasured and must pass the fixed paired promotion gates.
